cls: Antineoplastic - pan-HER (HER1/HER2/HER4) irreversible tyrosine kinase inhibitor
pharm: Irreversible covalent inhibitor of EGFR (HER1), HER2 and HER4; blocks downstream signalling and is active in HER2-positive disease including some trastuzumab-resistant settings
quick: 240 mg orally once daily for 1 year (extended adjuvant); loperamide prophylaxis mandatory initially
With food (improves tolerability and absorption consistency).
Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and after treatment per labeling
Do not breastfeed during treatment and after last dose per labeling
See full labeling; monitor renal function with diarrhoea/vomiting/dehydration risk
See full labeling; dose-reduce in moderate-severe impairment for hepatically cleared agents
No specific interaction; avoid excess with hepatotoxic or myelosuppressive therapy
CBC, LFTs, drug-specific toxicities, pregnancy status
summary: Neratinib (Nerlynx) is indicated for extended adjuvant treatment of HER2-positive early breast cancer after trastuzumab-based therapy, and with capecitabine for HER2-positive metastatic disease after 2+ anti-HER2 regimens. It is an irreversible pan-HER inhibitor; severe diarrhoea is near-universal without loperamide prophylaxis (given with the first cycle per labeling), alongside hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal risk.
indications: Extended adjuvant treatment of HER2-positive early-stage breast cancer after adjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy
HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer in combination with capecitabine after 2 or more prior anti-HER2 regimens in the metastatic setting

dosage.d: 240 mg once daily for 1 year, started within 1 year of completing trastuzumab
dosage.t: With food, at the same time daily; mandatory loperamide prophylaxis with the first cycle per labeling
dosage.n: Hold/reduce for grade 3+ diarrhoea or hepatotoxicity

dosage.d: 240 mg once daily days 1-21 with capecitabine 750 mg/m2 twice daily days 1-14 of each 21-day cycle

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Neratinib binds covalently and irreversibly to EGFR (HER1), HER2 and HER4, shutting down HER-family downstream proliferation signalling in HER2-positive breast cancer, including some trastuzumab-exposed disease.

monitor: LFTs monthly for 3 months then every 3 months

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (markedly reduce exposure - avoid)
moderate: Proton-pump inhibitors and H2 blockers (reduce neratinib solubility/absorption - avoid; separate antacids)
P-gp substrates with narrow index (neratinib inhibits P-gp)
interactions.food: With food (improves tolerability and absorption consistency).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

serious: Severe diarrhoea with dehydration, AKI and electrolyte disturbance
emergency: Severe diarrhoea with dizziness, fainting or reduced urine - seek urgent care
Yellowing of eyes/skin (liver injury) - seek urgent evaluation

monitoring: Diarrhoea grade and hydration at each early visit
counsel: Diarrhoea usually starts in the first days - take loperamide exactly as prescribed from day 1, plus diet and fluids
Avoid antacids/PPIs unless the team approves (they lower absorption); separate antacids by hours
Report yellowing of skin/eyes or severe abdominal pain
Use effective contraception; tell the team about new prescription or herbal medicines
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: Diarrhoea prophylaxis with loperamide for the first 1-2 cycles is labeling-mandated, not optional
Irreversible pan-HER binding gives prolonged target suppression but also EGFR-mediated GI/skin toxicity
Gastric-acid reducers meaningfully reduce absorption - a common adherence pitfall
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. Take as soon as remembered on the same day; do not double.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
